body:
`publish()` under `--no-issue` still treats a failed T4 as a flag:

```python
if not _t4_passes(cfg, d):
    if pending_id:
        print("… proceeding in --no-issue (pending-id) mode; the contribution is FLAGGED …")
```

The premise is that the one thing legitimately missing is the not-yet-assigned tracker id — but the gate is never told which mode it ran in, so the amnesty covers the **whole checker**: a malformed PR body, a broken commit-msg opener, anything `contribcheck` would have caught is waved through as "pending id".

The instance replaced this (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#184 review rounds) and defended it through the v0.56.0 merge (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#195): the mode is passed **into** the gate — `_t4_passes(…, pending_id=…)` exports `$PDCA_PENDING_ID=1` beside `$PDCA_BUNDLE`, derived from the flag and never inherited (an inherited value is scrubbed, not honoured), and the shipped checker reads it as `contribcheck --no-issue`: the tracker-id requirement drops, every other contribution check stays in force. What is left to fail is a real defect, and a real defect blocks the push in either mode. The relax branch is deleted outright.

Minor sibling in the same function, from the #338 rework: the immediate pre-run announce line (`· T4 gate <label> (a gate can take minutes; a heartbeat follows)…`) was dropped in favour of the heartbeat alone. #181's finding was specifically that the silence **before the first tick** reads as a hang on the very first thing publish does after its guards — the instance keeps the announce, and passes the heartbeat label unprefixed since the announce already says "T4 gate".
title: publish: --no-issue relaxes the WHOLE T4 verdict to a flag — pass the mode into the gate instead
